mainEntity.name: What are the main stages of building a home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A home addition project typically moves through architectural design, permitting, site preparation, foundation pouring, framing, exterior tie-ins, and interior finishing. Once plans pass municipal review, crews excavate and pour the slab or foundation before erecting walls and roof trusses. Exterior tie-ins ensure siding, roofing, or full-house stuccoing integrate seamlessly with your original structure. Interior work follows with rough-in plumbing, electrical, drywall installation, trim, and flooring. Project managers supervise each phase to coordinate trades and keep inspections moving smoothly toward final completion.
